title: Quant profile verifier with staged goldset and calibration checkpoints
creator: Maya Singh
description: Build an automated verifier that validates quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) against a staged reference prompt set and per-profile calibration checkpoints. The verifier will run three validation passes: quick smoke (latency and output sanity), cohorted regression checks (weighted metrics on representative user cohorts), and a production gate (pass/fail based on delta thresholds and rollback triggers). Deliverables: CI job, dashboard panels, test artifacts, and a documented runbook for triage.
acceptance_criteria: CI job runs on every quant-profile commit and produces a pass/fail artifact
Regression metrics computed: top-1 token match, n-gram ROUGE-L, embedding cosine stability, and calibration drift score
Staged goldset (three tiers: quick, representative, adversarial) stores outputs and baseline hashes in storage
Automatic fail gating enforces rollback for profiles exceeding configurable drift thresholds
Grafana dashboard shows per-profile histogram of metric deltas and a pass/fail summary panel
Runbook with playbook steps for investigating false positives and initiating manual overrides
comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Singh: Initial ticket created. Proposed three-tier validation (quick/repr/adv). Suggested metrics list and gating logic. Referenced existing calibration checkpoints from ENG-240001.

2026-02-23 Liam Chen: Spike complete for FP8 simulated quantization. Observed systematic token-shift on arithmetic prompts; added an adversarial cohort to capture this pattern. Decided to include embedding-stability metric to catch semantic drift.

2026-03-01 Devon Patel (ML): Reviewed metric choices. Recommended replacing BLEU with ROUGE-L for longer-span fidelity. Flagged potential variance from stochastic decoding—propose fixed-seed decode and multiple-sample aggregations.

2026-03-05 QA: Ran manual replay on representative cohort. Found intermittent flakiness around long-context LLMs; hypothesis: KV cache warmup and batching interactions. Action: record per-request batch size and warmup flag in telemetry.
2026-03-09 Design review (Anika Rao): UX for dashboard mockups approved with minor tweaks. Add a compact pass/fail indicator suitable for on-call alerts.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Implemented CI pipeline skeleton (Jenkins job + k8s job manifest). Pushed prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/4256. Telemetry backfilled for batch size slices.

2026-03-13 Maya Singh: Performance trade-off note: enabling exhaustive adversarial pass increases CI runtime from ~20m to ~3h. Plan: run adversarial nightly and keep quick/repr in PR gates. Drafted run scheduling in Confluence.
2026-03-13 Security (review): Verified no secrets are stored in artifacts. Request to record whether KMS-wrapped model weights were used in calibration steps for auditability. Marked for follow-up.

2026-03-13 Liam Chen: Next steps - finalize threshold defaults, wire alerting to PagerDuty for profile fails, and add heuristic for automatic rollback when both latency and accuracy regress beyond limits.
notes: Design trade-offs: strict gating prevents bad rollouts but increases developer iteration time. Chosen compromise: fast PR-level guards with conservative thresholds and nightly exhaustive runs that can trigger enforcement windows. Calibration checkpoints are immutable artifacts keyed by profile hash to ensure reproducible replays. Consider adding a canary policy that evaluates newly generated calibrations on a small percentage of live traffic before full rollout.
